land.text: the Nakdong basin of Byeonhan, whose states 'most ... joined' the Gaya confederacy

predecessors.note: Split from Cliopatria's Byeonhan row; see the byeonhan notes for the choice of 301.

land.text: the last Gaya land: Daegaya and the remaining polities of the Nakdong basin

successors.note: Geumgwan Gaya (Gimhae) went to Silla in 532 and the rest in 562; Cliopatria shows the Gimhae part in Silla's shape from 534 and the rest from 567.

capitals.name: Geumgwan Gaya (Gimhae)
capitals.note: No capital is named on the Gaya pages; Geumgwan Gaya, 'believed to have been located around the modern-day city of Gimhae', was 'the ruling state of the confederacy' until it 'was conquered in 532'. The dot marks the leading state, not a formal capital.

capitals.name: Daegaya (Goryeong)
capitals.note: 'Daegaya was located in present-day Goryeong County'; the Gaya page says the confederacy 'was revived around the turn of the 5th and 6th centuries' around Daegaya, and the Daegaya page that the 554 defeat cost Daegaya its leadership to Ara Gaya. The dot marks the leading state, not a formal capital.

correction.text: Cliopatria's Byeonhan shape in these years is Gaya's: 'in the Nakdong River basin of southern Korea', with Geumgwan Gaya at Gimhae and Daegaya at Goryeong

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 301-531, the years of the byeonhan_-91 shape that belong to Gaya (13,603 km2, 127.45-129.35E, 34.6-35.9N). The Gaya page gives no area; the shape covers the lower Nakdong, Gimhae (Geumgwan) and the upper-valley seat of Goryeong (Daegaya). The page also says the confederacy 'disintegrated under pressure from Goguryeo between 391 and 412', yet names Geumgwan conquered in 532 and Daegaya in 562, so the shape is held to 531. Unverified within the 301-531 span: page budget.

correction.text: the same shape (10,542 km2), held from 532, not 534: 'Geumgwan Gaya, the ruling state of the confederacy, was conquered in 532'

keyframe_review.note: 534..560 in Cliopatria; years change, not the outline. The shape lacks the Gimhae/Busan edge (127.45-128.81E against 129.35E before): 3,061 km2, which Silla gains in its own 534 shape (+3,113 km2). Cliopatria is two years late; the Geumgwan page says Geumgwan Gaya 'capitulated to Silla in 532 AD'.

correction.text: the same shape, held 561-562 only: 'Daegaya fell to the armies of Silla under general Kim Isabu in 562'

keyframe_review.note: 561..566 in Cliopatria (10,542 km2); the last Gaya polity fell in 562 ('the last holdout, Daegaya fell in 562', Gaya page), so 563-566 belong to Silla. Cliopatria's Silla shape grows by 11,108 km2 in 567 (75,507 to 86,616), about this shape's area, five years after the fall.

region.text: the Nakdong basin: 'formed a confederacy in the 2nd and 3rd centuries' around Geumgwan Gaya

ledger.note: 301: the Gaya confederacy takes over from Byeonhan around Gimhae. The Gaya page: 'some of the city-states of Byeonhan evolved into the Kaya confederacy'; 'scholars have identified the late 3rd century as a period of transition from Byeonhan to Kaya'; its legend has Suro, Geumgwan Gaya's king, descending 'in the year AD 42' and 'The traditional period ... is AD 42-532' (infobox '42 BCE-562 CE', sic). 301 is a bridge between the late 3rd century and the Byeonhan lead's '4th century'.

region.text: Geumgwan Gaya at the mouth of the Nakdong, 'around the modern-day city of Gimhae': the part of the 533 shape that Cliopatria's 534 shape no longer holds (13,603 - 10,542 = 3,061 km2)

ledger.note: 532: Geumgwan Gaya, the ruling state of Gaya, falls to Silla. 'Geumgwan Gaya, the ruling state of the confederacy, was conquered in 532' (Gaya page); 'After Geumgwan Gaya capitulated to Silla in 532 AD, its royal house was accepted into the Sillan aristocracy' (Geumgwan page). The region is the Gimhae part of the shape that Cliopatria's 534 shape drops.

region.text: the last holdout Daegaya at Goryeong and the remaining Gaya polities

ledger.note: 562: Daegaya falls and Gaya is gone. 'Daegaya fell to the armies of Silla under general Kim Isabu in 562', presented as punishment for the 554 alliance with Baekje; the Gaya page: 'the last Kaya polities remained independent until they were conquered by Silla in 562'.
562: the Gaya confederacy ends. 'the last holdout, Daegaya fell in 562'; the page's 'traditional period' of 42-532 stops at Geumgwan's fall.

wars.name: Goguryeo's pressure on Gaya
wars.outcome: The Gaya page says the confederacy 'disintegrated under pressure from Goguryeo between 391 and 412', yet the same page has Geumgwan conquered in 532 and Daegaya in 562.
wars.note: Kept so the reviewer sees the contradiction; no zone and no ledger event because no page places a campaign or a loss. The Gwanggaeto page (opened for Dongye) records Silla's rescue in 400 but no Gaya campaign.

wars.name: Silla's conquest of Gaya

zones.text: the Gaya shape, Geumgwan in 532 and Daegaya in 562

wars.outcome: Silla destroyed Takgitan Gaya in 529, took Geumgwan Gaya in 532 and Daegaya in 562; Gaya ended.
wars.note: Dated episodes: 'In 529, Silla destroyed Takgitan Gaya' (place not on the page, so no loss event); 532 and 562 (ledger); 'In 541 and 544, Paekche led the Sabi Conferences' to save Gaya; Gwansan Fortress 554 (Daegaya page). No contest event: the pages date four episodes, not a front.

wars.name: Battle of Gwansan Fortress
wars.outcome: Daegaya allied with Baekje against Silla; both sides took heavy losses, Daegaya lost the leadership of Gaya to Ara Gaya and fell eight years later.
wars.note: 'Daegaya allied with Baekje against Silla at the battle of Gwansan Fortress in 554'; the page presents the 562 conquest as punishment for the alliance.

certainty.note: A confederacy of city-states in river valleys with no frontier on any page; the Cliopatria outline is a block of the lower Nakdong. The 532 and 562 conquests are dated, but the lines are not.

notes: Split off Cliopatria's Byeonhan row (cliopatria_names ['Byeonhan']; the byeonhan dossier keeps -91..300). The 301 start and the Byeonhan/Gaya boundary are at confidence 1 (see byeonhan notes): the pages give 42, the 2nd and 3rd centuries, c. 209, the late 3rd century and the 4th century. The Gaya page also says the confederacy was 'revived around the turn of the 5th and 6th centuries' around Daegaya and 'disintegrated under pressure from Goguryeo between 391 and 412'; the drawn shape is held whole to 531 because no page places a loss before Takgitan (529, no place) and Geumgwan (532). The Japanese 'Mimana' claim (Nihon Shoki: Kaya as a Yamato outpost, 300-710) is on the Gaya page as 'largely refuted since the 1970s' and is not used. Cliopatria ends the row in 566, four years after Daegaya fell, and moves Gimhae to Silla in 534, two years after 532; both keyframes are adjusted by years only. This dossier overlaps the additions batch jk-02-x's remit (Gaya is a state Cliopatria lacks as a row of its own); it was written here because it is split from a row of this batch, so jk-02-x should skip it. Region names: none unresolved. Page budget: 5 pages (the new state of a split row, 2-5 allowed for new dossiers).
